SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY rand DESC;
3.2.3 reserves `rand` in order position, answering `ORDER BY rand` with "Unexpected token `;`, expected (" — only the `ORDER BY RAND()` call form is accepted, so a bare `rand` here must stay refused
SELECT * FROM person WHERE NOT deleted;

3.2.3 has no prefix `NOT` at all, only the `not(...)` builtin: `Unexpected token 'an identifier', expected Eof` pointing at `deleted`. `NOT (deleted)` and `not(deleted)` are unaffected — both lex as the call.
RETURN NOT true;
Same as the idiom case, on a bare literal: `Unexpected token `true`, expected Eof`. Only `NOT (...)`/`not(...)` parse.
FOR $x IN user:1..user:9 { RETURN $x; };

A *record range* — two full record ids joined by `..` — never parses on 3.2.3, in FOR or anywhere else: `Unexpected token `:`, expected {` (verified identically in RETURN, SELECT FROM and LET). `user:1..` is always the start of that record id's own embedded id range, which takes a plain id value, not another whole `tb:id`.
FOR $x IN (user:1..user:9) { RETURN $x; };
Parentheses do not help — same construct, `Unexpected token `:` expected delimiter `)``.
DEFINE FIELD f ON t FLEXIBLE TYPE object;

3.2.3: `Parse error: FLEXIBLE must be specified after TYPE`. This is the clause order the published docs show, so it is the one every FLEXIBLE user reaches for; the engine takes only `TYPE object FLEXIBLE`.
DEFINE FUNCTION fn::greet($name) { RETURN $name; };
3.2.3: `Unexpected token ')', expected :` — every `fn::` parameter needs an explicit `: <kind>`. A closure's parameter (`|$v| $v`) is unaffected; only `DEFINE FUNCTION`'s own list requires the type.
DEFINE FIELD f ON t TYPE geometry<pointt>;

3.2.3: `Unexpected token 'an identifier', expected a geometry kind name`. The seven names (`point`, `line`, `polygon`, `multipoint`, `multiline`, `multipolygon`, `collection`) are a closed set; anything else is a parse error, not a semantic one.
